newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German July state inflation data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German July state inflation data.

text.p: The following is a reaction by economists to the first two sets of German state inflation data for the month of July which showed a slight increase from the previous month. The state of Bavaria reported its July prices rose 0.5 percent on the month and 1.7 percent on the year, compared with a 0.2 percent rise on the month and a 1.6 percent rise on the year in June. The state of Hesse reported its numbers earlier this morning.
ARMIN KAYSER, economist at SBC Warburg in Frankfurt: "These numbers are not wholly perfect, they have climbed and I think this reflects the depreciation of the mark."

Armin Kayser "Slowly the depreciation of the mark is filtering into the cost of living rates. This development is reflected most vividly in the sharp increase in services. On the other hand we see rather stable developments in domestic prices such as rents and other things. Looking ahead we expect to see a small blip in inflation rates in the coming months, but this is still nothing to get overly worried about. I think the Bundesbank will not do anything in terms of adjusting interest rates however to react to these numbers. It would not be wise to raise interest rates now while the domestic economy is still struggling to recover."

HOLGER FAHRINKRUG, senior Germany economist at UBS in Frankfurt however disagreed that the mark's depreciation was reflected in July inflation data. "The lower mark is not at all filtering through to the inflation prices. The slight blip higher seen in the data is solely related to an increase in the amount of contributions Germans need to pay for medications. Import prices, as reflected in the food prices, electricity and mineral oil, to a large extent, remain under control and are in fact still below the average rates seen for this year. The rise in prices was caused by one-offs. There is absolutely no reason to be concerned about inflation levels.
